body.statement: For every finite \(X\), fixed \(\ell\), finite \(\mathcal I\ni\varnothing\), and loopless graph pair \(G,H\), \(\mathcal P_{\mathcal I}(G)\subseteq\mathcal P_{\mathcal I}(H)\) if and only if \(\operatorname{Cover}_{\mathcal I}(G,H)\). Consequently, \(\mathcal P_{\mathcal I}(G)=\mathcal P_{\mathcal I}(H)\) if and only if both \(\operatorname{Cover}_{\mathcal I}(G,H)\) and \(\operatorname{Cover}_{\mathcal I}(H,G)\) hold. This criterion is exact on lower-dimensional rank, cancellation, nullification, invisible-source, and source-symmetry strata, and it is a finite graph-generated compatibility representation rather than the original structural-existence formula.
body.justification: The theorem gives the exact equality functional for full joint response-kernel sets under one coefficient matrix and one unrestricted source tuple.
body.gap: Neither observational zero-allowed equivalence nor acyclic graphical intervention equivalence supplies the exact-support cyclic common-mechanism criterion.
body.consumer: Perturbational analyses can enumerate all exact-support latent feedback mechanisms compatible with the complete population intervention tuple.
body.proof_tex:
We prove directed containment.  Suppose first that
\(\mathcal P_{\mathcal I}(G)\subseteq\mathcal P_{\mathcal I}(H)\), and fix \(C\in\mathcal D_G\).  By \(\text{thm:exact-mixing-realization}\), there is an exact-support matrix \(Q=I_N-B\) on \(G\), with all required principal systems invertible, whose observed mixing matrix is \(C\).  Equip its visible columns with the independent two-point diagnostic sources \(\xi^C\) from \(\text{lem:diagnostic-mixture-rigidity}\), and equip its zero columns with arbitrary independent nonconstant non-Gaussian sources.  The broadened exact-support model class imposes no location or moment restriction, so this is an admissible \(G\)-mechanism.

By the assumed containment, its complete kernel tuple is generated by one admissible \(H\)-mechanism; denote that mechanism's observed mixing matrix by \(D\) and its common source vector by \(\eta\).  Exact mixing realization gives \(D\in\mathcal D_H\).  Equality of the observational kernels is
\[
 \mathcal L(C\xi^C)=\mathcal L(D\eta).
\]
The diagnostic rigidity lemma therefore supplies a surjection \(f:U_C\twoheadrightarrow U_D\) and nonzero \(a_i\) such that
\[
 C_{:,i}=a_iD_{:,f(i)}\qquad(i\in U_C).                              \tag{9}
\]

Fix \(S\in\mathcal I\).  By the intervention-pushforward lemma, the two equal kernels have representations
\[
 K_S(x)=\tau_{T_S(C)x}\mu_{C,S}
       =\tau_{T_S(D)x}\mu_{D,S},
 \qquad
 \mu_{C,S}=\mathcal L(R_S(C)\xi^C),\quad
 \mu_{D,S}=\mathcal L(R_S(D)\eta).
\]
At \(x=0\), the two residual laws agree.  The translation-rigidity lemma then gives \(T_S(C)=T_S(D)\), including the empty-output case.  Thus \((D,f,a)\) satisfies every clause of \(\operatorname{Cover}_{\mathcal I}(G,H)\).

Conversely, assume \(\operatorname{Cover}_{\mathcal I}(G,H)\) and take an arbitrary admissible \(G\)-mechanism with observed mixing matrix \(C\) and source vector \(\varepsilon\).  Exact mixing realization places \(C\) in \(\mathcal D_G\).  Select a cover witness \((D,f,a)\).  The same realization theorem constructs an admissible exact-support coefficient matrix on \(H\) with observed mixing matrix \(D\).  For every \(j\in U_D\), put
\[
 \eta_j=\sum_{i:f(i)=j}a_i\varepsilon_i.                             \tag{10}
\]
The fibers are nonempty and disjoint, so these sources are mutually independent.  They are nonconstant by \(\text{lem:independent-sum-nondegenerate}\), and they are non-Gaussian by \(\text{lem:levy-cramer-decomposition}\): a Gaussian sum would force every nonconstant summand to be Gaussian.  Add arbitrary independent legal sources on the zero columns of \(D\).  This constructs one admissible target source tuple, with no appeal to means or variances.  Equation (9) gives \(C\varepsilon=D\eta\).

For every \(S\), equality of the response matrices and (9) imply, column by column,
\[
 R_S(C)_{:,i}
 =C_{X\setminus S,i}-T_S(C)C_{S,i}
 =a_iR_S(D)_{:,f(i)}\qquad(i\in U_C).                               \tag{11}
\]
If \(i\notin U_C\), then \(C_{:,i}=0\), and the intervention-pushforward lemma gives \(R_S(C)_{:,i}=0\).  Surjectivity of \(f\), (10), and (11) therefore give
\[
 R_S(C)\varepsilon=R_S(D)\eta.
\]
Together with \(T_S(C)=T_S(D)\), equation (7) proves equality of the two kernels for every \(x\), using the same \(D\) and the same \(\eta\) in all regimes.  Hence
\[
 \mathcal P_{\mathcal I}(G)\subseteq\mathcal P_{\mathcal I}(H)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \operatorname{Cover}_{\mathcal I}(G,H).
\]
Applying the directed statement in both orders proves the equality criterion.  Exact mixing realization retains every punctured-fiber and Hall--Rado boundary, while the diagnostic lemma retains zero columns, proportional columns, source symmetries, and lower-dimensional cancellations.  Thus no generic, closure, centering, or moment condition has entered the population equivalence theorem.
